critiques.target: H4 / H4.2 (decision instrument), E098, E100–E105 off-seed verdicts
critiques.issue: Pairing by seed does not reduce variance here, but the loop still computes SEs as if it did. E028 shows the same seed rerun in a new process moves by -0.27/+0.19/-0.59 pp, which is about as much as cross-seed sd (0.22-0.38). cuDNN-pick divergence breaks the pairing. So E098's 'paired SE 0.05 pp' is wrong. The real SE of a single-process 22-seed paired difference is about 0.35·√2/√22 ≈ 0.10-0.11 pp. Measured that way, every off-seed delta since E096 is under 1.2 SE: E100 +0.09, E102 0.00, E103 +0.02, E104 +0.12, E105 +0.09. E098 found that one process per arm cannot resolve 0.1 pp, then E100-E105 were each decided on one process per arm. E101 also shows 3-seed run sd of ~0.2 pp, above the 0.1-0.15 that H4 states.
critiques.suggestion: Update H4: run sd of the 3-seed mean is ~0.2 pp, and paired off-seed SE is ~0.1 pp per process. Mark E100, E102, E103, E104 and E105 inconclusive. Require at least 3 processes per arm (seeds 3-26) before any keep or close. At ~2 min per process that is affordable. First measure the within-seed cross-process sd directly from the E094/E098 checksums and logs.

critiques.target: E096 keep (H2.11.4 E096~) and the E100 lineage
critiques.issue: E096 was kept with --force on one effective sample: E096 and E097 are bit-identical. That breaks H4's own rule a third time, after E090. Its +0.17 pp off-seed came from one process. In E098 the same code scored 0.7514 off-seed, -0.11 pp against E090 run in parallel. So the window pin has no net support, yet the current tip (E100) inherits it, and every comparison after E100 uses it as the base.
critiques.suggestion: Record E096 as unresolved: the scored pool counts once and the off-seed results conflict (+0.17 / -0.11). Before stacking anything else, run a multi-process E090 vs E096 vs E100 comparison, so the window pin and the 32 px lr×1.25 are each tested on their own.

critiques.target: E100 kept as tip / H10.2.1 'supports weakly'
critiques.issue: The tip rests on two distinct scored samples, 0.7561 and 0.7516: a 0.45 pp spread with mean 0.7538, about 0.04 above the gate. With run sd ~0.2, roughly a third of reruns would fail. E105, raising the lr everywhere, showed the same +0.09 pp off-seed and was called noise and refuted. E100's +0.09 was called support and kept. The two thresholds are not applied the same way.
critiques.suggestion: Use one bar for both: E100 and E105 are both inconclusive. Treat E100 as feasible by luck, as the loop did for E090. The path-length mechanism (H10.2) is still untested. If it is retested, also run the matched E105 arm (global ×1.25, on E090 not E100) so 'phase-local' and 'just a higher lr' can be told apart.

critiques.issue: The evidence tokens are inverted. H10.1.1 predicted an off-seed gain of +0.05 to +0.15 pp, and E104 gave +0.12, inside that band, yet it is logged as E104-. H11.2.1 predicted ≤ +0.03 and said a result ≥ +0.08 refutes it, yet it is still open with no token. E104's scored run (0.7525) is also 0.13 pp below the tip's scored pool, so the scored and off-seed results disagree in sign.
critiques.suggestion: Change it to H10.1.1 E104~ (leaning supports) and H11.2.1 E104~ (leaning refutes). Do not let it count as a real refutation until a multi-process replicate exists. Lower H11.2's confidence.

critiques.target: H6.5.4 (E103 marked refutes) and H6 retirement
critiques.issue: By its own pre-registration, H6.5.4 is refuted only if the result is ≤ -0.05 pp. E103 gave +0.00 against E090 and +0.02 against the tip, which falls in the dead zone, so it is inconclusive. It was also run on E100, not on the E090 config the hypothesis named. Compared with E081 (-0.09 with copied buffers), buffer averaging moved the 20-step window by about +0.1 pp. That is weakly in the direction of explanation (b), BN mismatch, not against it. The outcome note 'End-of-run averaging closed' overstates what was found.
critiques.suggestion: Re-mark it E103~. H6 can still be retired on expected value, but record the reason as 'not worth more runs', not 'the BN-mismatch mechanism is refuted'.

critiques.target: H11 (late full-res exposure binds) and H11.1.1

critiques.suggestion: Lower H11 to ~0.25. Either run the never-freeze arm in multiple processes or drop the H11.1 mechanism. Note that H11.1.1's closing clause points back to early-phase fragility (see the H8 critique).

critiques.issue: The three largest clean negative effects since Muon arrived are all early-phase interventions: E032 (no 24 px bridge, -0.68), E043 (bs 2048 early, -0.49) and E093 (whitening bias frozen at ~3%, -0.44 off-seed and -0.5 scored). That is a consistent pattern and the strongest structural signal in the tree, yet H8 was retired. E104's 'early steps are not worth more' conclusion comes from one process. critiques.target: H1 'zero-cost levers exhausted' carried into the Muon regime / H6
critiques.issue: Augmentation was only tested under SGD at 8 epochs: brightness/contrast (E008) and crop vs resize (E016). Muon fits ~1.1 pp better and the tail adds averaging, so the regularization balance has changed. H1 itself warns that its 'no retuning' lesson does not carry over to Muon. critiques.target: H2 time levers: plateau and untried structure (H2.18, capacity reallocation)

Reallocating capacity under Muon was never tried either: narrower group 1 at 31×31, which is energy-heavy at 32 px, with group 3 widened at equal cost. E005 and E017 were SGD-era tests.
critiques.suggestion: Run H2.18.1's untimed per-variant profile next, before any scored run. Add one untimed per-layer energy profile at 32 px to rank groups by J/step, then test a cost-neutral width reallocation. Stop proposing schedule or batch reshuffles.

critiques.issue: E098 found that E096's seeds 3-10 gave 0.7543 in one process and 0.7518 in another: a 0.25 pp gap on the same 8 seeds. E101 found 0.45 pp between identical-code scored runs. Per-seed rerun sd of ~0.35 can account for this (≈0.17 pp sd on an 8-seed rerun difference), so a per-process offset is not required. But H4.5.1, the kernel-name logging that would test it, was requested in E081/E094/E098/E099 and never reported. E099 changed the pick sets and its kernel diff is not reported either.

structured_output.summary:
The loop's decision instrument is broken, and every verdict since E096 rests on it. The same seed rerun in a new process moves by about as much as cross-seed sd (E028), so seed-paired off-seed differences have an SE of ~0.1 pp per process, not the 0.05 claimed in E098. Every recent delta (+0.09, +0.12, 0.00, +0.02, +0.09) is inside noise. Even so, E096 (one bit-identical sample, contradicted in E098) and E100 (distinct scored 0.7561 and 0.7516) were kept on single favorable draws. That is the same luck-selection H4 warns about, and the tip is likely feasible only by luck.

The verdicts are also applied inconsistently. E100's +0.09 counted as support while E105's identical +0.09 counted as noise. E104 is logged as refuting H10.1.1 although it landed inside that hypothesis's predicted band, and its rival H11.2.1 has no token at all. E103 fell inside its own pre-registered dead zone, but averaging was declared 'closed'. Seven Lvl3s with decisive tokens remain 'open', and the H2 and H4 Lvl1 text still describes E090 as current.

Substantively, two things hold:
- **Time search has converged.** Every remaining trade (trims, the 28 px substitution, added steps anywhere) runs at ~0.04-0.065 pp per 1% of time, and there is no margin left to spend.
- **The strongest structural signal is being ignored.** Early-training damage is large (E032 -0.68, E043 -0.49, E093 -0.44), yet H8 is retired.

Directions never tried in the Muon regime:
- augmentation (translate magnitude, cutout late)
- class-balanced batches
- schedule shape (WSD/cosine)
- capacity reallocation across groups
- the untimed depth-cut profile (H2.18.1)
- the PCIe judge projection

**Next steps:**
1. Recompute SEs with within-seed cross-process variance.
2. Re-decide E090, E096 and E100 with at least 3 processes each.
3. Fix the tokens and statuses.
4. Spend further runs only on structural accuracy sources with an expected gain of at least 0.15 pp, or on the depth-cut profile.
